provenance_note: Mixed status: source_checked means an editorial source cross-check, not peer or expert review. Other primitives remain unverified candidates. No external bulk data copied.

items.name: Exponential Time Hypothesis
items.definition: The conjecture that 3-SAT has no deterministic 2^{o(n)}-time algorithm in the number n of variables.
items.scope_note: Conjecture, not established lower bound.

items.name: IID Samples
items.definition: Samples are independent and identically distributed from a fixed target distribution.
items.scope_note: Violations include distribution shift and dependent sampling.

items.name: Independent Private Values
items.definition: An auction environment in which bidder values are privately known and independent under a common prior.
items.scope_note: Independence need not imply identical distribution; risk assumptions are separate.

items.name: Neighboring Datasets
items.definition: Two inputs related by a specified record insertion, deletion or replacement convention.
items.scope_note: Adjacency is part of the DP definition and must be explicit.

items.name: No Overbidding
items.definition: A restriction excluding strategies that bid above stated values according to a specific valuation and bidding convention.
items.scope_note: Used in some auction-efficiency analyses; its formal meaning differs across mechanisms.

items.name: Quasilinear Utility
items.definition: Preferences in which utility equals valuation of the allocation minus the payment, or plus a transfer.
items.scope_note: Standard in mechanism design but excludes income-dependent marginal utility of money.

items.name: Realizability
items.definition: There exists a hypothesis in the chosen class having zero population error in the stated learning problem.
items.scope_note: Contrasts with agnostic learning.

items.name: Resource Augmentation
items.definition: An analysis model in which an algorithm is given additional resources relative to its comparison benchmark.
items.scope_note: State the specific resource such as machine speed, memory or capacity and augmentation parameter.

items.name: Single-Edge Deletion
items.definition: Perturbation comparing a graph with the graph after removing one edge.
items.scope_note: Not the same as edge-weight change or vertex removal.

items.name: Single-Vertex Deletion
items.definition: Perturbation comparing a graph with a graph after removing one vertex and its incident edges.
items.scope_note: May change much more information than single edge deletion.

items.name: Strong Exponential Time Hypothesis
items.definition: The conjecture that for k-CNF-SAT, the optimal exponential-time base approaches 2 as clause width k grows.
items.scope_note: Fine-grained conjecture, not a proved theorem; distinguish ETH.

items.name: Submodular Valuations
items.definition: Set valuations satisfy diminishing marginal returns: the marginal value of an item cannot increase when the current bundle grows.
items.scope_note: Assumes a ground set and an appropriate nondecreasing/normalized convention when invoking combinatorial-auction guarantees.

items.name: Unknown Prediction Quality
items.definition: The algorithm is not given the magnitude of the prediction error as an input parameter.
items.scope_note: Error may appear in the analysis even when unknown to the algorithm.

items.name: XOS Valuations
items.definition: Set valuations expressible as the pointwise maximum of a collection of additive valuations.
items.scope_note: Also called fractionally subadditive under standard nonnegative monotone valuation assumptions.

items.name: First-Price Auction
items.definition: A sealed-bid single-item auction where the highest bidder wins and pays their own bid.
items.scope_note: The single-item standard should be distinguished from simultaneous/sequential multi-item compositions.

items.name: Second-Price Auction
items.definition: A sealed-bid single-item auction where the highest bidder wins and pays the second-highest bid.
items.scope_note: Truthful bidding is weakly dominant under standard private-value assumptions without allocation externalities.

items.name: Sequential First-Price Auction
items.definition: A sequential composition of first-price auctions with bidding adapted to previous auction outcomes.
items.scope_note: Dynamic strategy spaces and sequential information distinguish it from simultaneous auctions.

items.name: Simultaneous First-Price Auction
items.definition: A composition of single-item first-price auctions run simultaneously for distinct items.
items.scope_note: This is a multi-item mechanism and not identical to a single-item first-price auction.

items.name: BPP
items.definition: The class of decision languages decidable by randomized polynomial-time algorithms with bounded two-sided error.
items.scope_note: Bounded error can be amplified.

items.name: coNP
items.definition: The class of complements of decision languages in NP.
items.scope_note: Whether NP equals coNP is open.

items.name: EXP
items.definition: The class of decision languages decidable in deterministic time 2^{poly(n)}.
items.scope_note: Do not confuse EXP with NEXP.

items.name: FPT
items.definition: Parameterized problems solvable in time f(k) times n^{O(1)}, where k is the parameter.
items.scope_note: A class of parameterized problems, not directly comparable to P without specifying parametrization.

items.name: NP
items.definition: The class of decision languages with polynomial-size witnesses verifiable in deterministic polynomial time.
items.scope_note: NP does not mean non-polynomial.

items.name: P
items.definition: The class of decision languages decidable by a deterministic Turing machine in polynomial time.
items.scope_note: Decision-problem convention.

items.name: PLS
items.definition: A class of total search problems reducible to finding local optima in implicitly specified finite neighborhoods.
items.scope_note: Finding a local optimum may be computationally intractable despite guaranteed existence.

items.name: PPAD
items.definition: A subclass of TFNP based on finding an endpoint in an implicitly represented directed graph under a parity argument.
items.scope_note: Search-problem class; do not confuse with a decision language class.

items.name: PSPACE
items.definition: The class of decision languages decidable using polynomial space by a deterministic Turing machine.
items.scope_note: Time can be exponential.

items.name: RP
items.definition: Randomized polynomial-time decision languages with one-sided error on YES instances and zero error on NO instances.
items.scope_note: Exact error-convention orientation matters.

items.name: XP
items.definition: Parameterized problems solvable in time n^{f(k)} for some computable f.
items.scope_note: FPT is contained in XP.

items.name: ZPP
items.definition: Decision languages with expected polynomial-time randomized algorithms that never return an incorrect answer.
items.scope_note: Equivalent to RP ∩ coRP under standard definitions.

items.name: Bayesian Nash Equilibrium
items.definition: A profile of type-contingent strategies in a Bayesian game where each type maximizes expected utility given its information and beliefs.
items.scope_note: Requires a specified type space, prior and information structure.

items.name: Coarse Correlated Equilibrium
items.definition: A distribution over action profiles with no profitable deviation to any fixed alternative action chosen without observing recommendations.
items.scope_note: No-external-regret learning may approach the coarse correlated equilibrium set under suitable conditions.

items.name: Correlated Equilibrium
items.definition: A joint distribution over action profiles for which obeying a privately observed recommendation is optimal against unilateral deviations.
items.scope_note: Weaker than requiring players' actions to be independent.

items.name: Mean Field Equilibrium
items.definition: A fixed point between an agent's optimal response to the population distribution and the population distribution generated by the agents.
items.scope_note: Formulation varies across continuous and discrete time; existence is model-dependent.

items.name: Mixed Nash Equilibrium
items.definition: A product distribution over players' strategies in which each mixed strategy maximizes expected payoff against the others.
items.scope_note: Distinguish finite games, which have existence results, from infinite strategy spaces requiring extra conditions.

items.name: Pure Nash Equilibrium
items.definition: A deterministic strategy profile from which no player can improve utility by a unilateral deviation.
items.scope_note: Existence is not guaranteed for every game.

items.name: Wardrop Equilibrium
items.definition: A feasible nonatomic flow in which each used path has minimum latency among feasible paths for the same origin-destination pair.
items.scope_note: Requires routing feasibility and the same demand classes to compare paths.

items.name: Batch-to-Online Transformation
items.definition: A reduction transforming offline approximation/stability properties into online regret or competitive performance.
items.scope_note: Random-order assumptions and sensitivity hypotheses affect guarantees.

items.name: Generalized Binary Tree Mechanism
items.definition: A private algorithm design framework extending the binary tree aggregation method to recursively separable graph problems.
items.scope_note: Depends on graph separator structure and weight adjacency.

items.name: Learning-Augmented Algorithms
items.definition: An algorithmic paradigm combining learned advice with traditional provable worst-case or error-sensitive guarantees.
items.scope_note: Consistency and robustness are separately quantified relative to a baseline.

items.name: Ordered Graph Limits
items.definition: Study limits of large dense graphs equipped with an ordering on vertices, using analytic orderon-type objects.
items.scope_note: Ordered limit theory is not equivalent to ordinary graphons because vertex order is substantive.

items.name: Shifting Mechanism
items.definition: A mechanism design approach using transformations or shifts to obtain differentially private combinatorial solutions.
items.scope_note: Established for cuts in a specific paper; do not apply universally to all graph problems.

items.name: Smoothed Analysis
items.definition: Analyze algorithmic performance when an adversarial input is modified by a specified random perturbation.
items.scope_note: Perturbation distribution and magnitude determine the model.

items.name: Smoothness Framework
items.definition: The method of bounding equilibrium inefficiency using smoothness inequalities, often extending beyond pure Nash equilibrium.
items.scope_note: Extensions require the relevant hypotheses for the equilibrium or learning concept.

items.name: Atomic Congestion Game
items.definition: A finite-player unweighted congestion game in which each player selects a resource subset and pays the sum of resource-specific costs based on integer user counts.
items.scope_note: Uses Rosenthal's unweighted resource-cost setting; heterogeneous player weights require a different model.

items.name: Congestion Game
items.definition: An umbrella family of games where players select resources and their costs depend on aggregate usage of the selected resources.
items.scope_note: Distinguish finite unweighted, weighted, atomic splittable and nonatomic variants; Rosenthal's theorem applies to finite unweighted games.

items.name: Mean Field Game
items.definition: A model for interactions of a large population of strategic agents through an aggregate distribution or state.
items.scope_note: Continuous-time, discrete-time and finite-state formulations have different equilibrium conditions.

items.name: Network Congestion Game
items.definition: A congestion game in which feasible strategies are paths in a network and resources are edges or arcs.
items.scope_note: Specify whether flows are atomic, weighted, splittable or nonatomic.

items.name: Nonatomic Congestion Game
items.definition: A congestion game modeled by divisible flows of infinitesimal agents whose individual actions do not change aggregate congestion.
items.scope_note: The standard routing equilibrium notion is Wardrop equilibrium; it is not literally finite pure Nash equilibrium.

items.name: Potential Game
items.definition: A game admitting a potential function whose changes are aligned with incentives for unilateral deviations.
items.scope_note: Exact, weighted and ordinal potentials are different notions; finite exact potential games have pure Nash equilibria.

items.name: Singleton Congestion Game
items.definition: A congestion game in which each strategy consists of exactly one resource.
items.scope_note: Equilibrium conclusions depend on the exact weighted or unweighted variant.

items.name: Weighted Congestion Game
items.definition: A finite congestion game where players contribute heterogeneous positive weights to the loads of the resources they select.
items.scope_note: Pure Nash equilibria may fail to exist without restrictions; weighted is not interchangeable with Rosenthal's unweighted model.

items.name: Bipartite Graph
items.definition: An undirected graph whose vertices split into two sets with all edges crossing between them.
items.scope_note: Equivalent to having no odd cycle for undirected graphs.

items.name: Bounded-Treewidth Graph
items.definition: A graph belonging to a graph family whose treewidth is bounded by a constant independent of graph size.
items.scope_note: Requires a specified bound when stating running-time results.

items.name: Chordal Graph
items.definition: An undirected graph with no induced cycle of length four or more.
items.scope_note: This is a hereditary class.

items.name: Complete Graph
items.definition: A simple undirected graph in which every pair of distinct vertices is adjacent.
items.scope_note: The graph on n vertices is often denoted K_n.

items.name: Forest
items.definition: An undirected graph with no cycles; equivalently each component is a tree.
items.scope_note: Finite simple graphs assumed.

items.name: Interval Graph
items.definition: The intersection graph of a family of intervals on a line.
items.scope_note: Every interval graph is chordal; the converse need not hold.

items.name: Perfect Graph
items.definition: A graph in which every induced subgraph has chromatic number equal to clique number.
items.scope_note: Perfectness is stronger than the equality only for the whole graph.

items.name: Planar Graph
items.definition: A graph that admits an embedding in the plane with no edge crossings except at shared endpoints.
items.scope_note: A graph property, not the same object as a particular planar embedding.

items.name: Series-Parallel Graph
items.definition: A graph constructible by recursive series and parallel composition under an explicitly chosen series-parallel convention.
items.scope_note: Several nonidentical definitions exist for directed, two-terminal and undirected forms.

items.name: Tree
items.definition: A connected undirected graph with no cycles.
items.scope_note: This entry uses finite undirected simple graph conventions.

items.name: Algorithmic Sensitivity
items.definition: A cross-cutting analysis of how much an algorithm's output or output distribution changes after an allowed small input perturbation.
items.scope_note: Distinct from the sensitivity of a numeric DP query; state perturbation and output metric.

items.name: Algorithmic Stability Lens
items.definition: A lens demanding stable outputs or behaviors when related input instances are perturbed.
items.scope_note: Can refer to distinct metrics such as average sensitivity and Lipschitz continuity.

items.name: Differential Privacy Lens
items.definition: A cross-cutting requirement that an algorithm satisfy a formal differential privacy guarantee for neighboring inputs.
items.scope_note: Graph adjacency model and privacy parameters determine what is protected.

items.name: Fault Tolerance Lens
items.definition: A lens requiring structural or algorithmic guarantees to survive a bounded number of specified faults.
items.scope_note: Specify edge versus vertex faults, budget and surviving guarantee.

items.name: Prediction Lens
items.definition: A cross-cutting approach using an externally supplied estimate or distribution to improve an algorithm while retaining an explicit guarantee for inaccurate advice.
items.scope_note: Predicted quantity, accuracy measure, baseline and robustness must be specified.

items.name: Replicability Lens
items.definition: A lens studying whether runs on independent samples using shared internal randomness agree with high probability.
items.scope_note: Different from privacy and input-output sensitivity, even if related.

items.name: Adjacency Matrix Model
items.definition: Graph oracle model allowing adjacency queries for any vertex pair.
items.scope_note: Distance normally uses the fraction of possible edges and differs from bounded-degree access.

items.name: Adversarial Online Model
items.definition: An online input model where requests are controlled by an adversary subject to stated adaptivity and information rules.
items.scope_note: Oblivious and adaptive adversaries differ for randomized algorithms.

items.name: Agnostic PAC Learning
items.definition: A PAC-style model requiring a hypothesis whose risk approaches the best attainable in a specified hypothesis class.
items.scope_note: Does not assume perfect realizability.

items.name: Bootstrap Percolation
items.definition: A spreading process in which infected nodes persist and healthy nodes become infected when enough neighbors are already infected.
items.scope_note: The infection threshold and time horizon must be specified.

items.name: Bounded-Degree Graph Model
items.definition: Graph oracle model with bounded vertex degree and indexed-neighbor queries.
items.scope_note: Distance is usually normalized by degree bound and number of vertices.

items.name: Cache-Oblivious Model
items.definition: Model requiring algorithms independent of cache parameters while evaluating block-transfer efficiency.
items.scope_note: Often assumes an ideal cache and a tall-cache property.

items.name: Cell-Probe Model
items.definition: Data-structure complexity model charging memory-cell accesses but not local computation.
items.scope_note: Cell size, space budget and update setting matter.

items.name: CONGEST Model
items.definition: A synchronous distributed graph model with O(log n)-bit messages per edge per round in the usual formulation.
items.scope_note: Bandwidth bound and initial knowledge must be stated.

items.name: Continual Release Model
items.definition: A privacy model requiring an algorithm to release intermediate results as a data stream or graph evolves.
items.scope_note: Privacy composition and the distinction between event-level and user-level adjacency matter.

items.name: Dense Graph Model
items.definition: Property testing model representing graphs by adjacency oracle queries with edge-fraction distance.
items.scope_note: Dense and bounded-degree models are not interchangeable.

items.name: Distribution Testing Model
items.definition: Sample access model for testing properties of an unknown probability distribution.
items.scope_note: Support size, metric and optional probability-evaluation oracles affect bounds.

items.name: Distributional Prediction
items.definition: Advice model supplying a probability distribution over unknown outcomes or inputs.
items.scope_note: Different from single point advice; distributional errors require a transport or divergence measure.

items.name: Dynamic Data Structure
items.definition: Structure supporting updates and queries over an evolving collection.
items.scope_note: Specify worst-case, amortized or randomized complexity separately.

items.name: Edge Differential Privacy
items.definition: Graph differential privacy where neighbors differ by an allowed edge insertion or deletion.
items.scope_note: Privacy does not automatically cover removal of all edges incident to a person.

items.name: Edge-Weight Differential Privacy
items.definition: Graph differential privacy where neighboring weighted graphs differ in one bounded edge-weight change.
items.scope_note: Can keep graph topology public; differs from edge-existence adjacency.

items.name: Edge-Weight Privacy
items.definition: A graph-private input model protecting bounded modifications to edge weights while retaining a specified public topology.
items.scope_note: Not identical to edge insertion/deletion privacy.

items.name: External Memory Model
items.definition: Model charging transfers between limited fast memory and block-based external storage.
items.scope_note: Internal memory and block size are explicit parameters.

items.name: Finite Automaton
items.definition: A finite-state machine that processes strings and accepts according to its transition rules.
items.scope_note: Deterministic and nondeterministic variants recognize regular languages.

items.name: Fractional Online Matching
items.definition: An online bipartite allocation model assigning fractional amounts to matching edges subject to capacity constraints.
items.scope_note: Distinct from integral matching; online advice and dual constraints alter guarantees.

items.name: Identical Parallel Machines
items.definition: A scheduling environment with multiple machines that process each job at the same rate.
items.scope_note: Whether preemption, migration and job release dates are allowed must be specified.

items.name: Insertion-Only Stream
items.definition: A data stream in which updates add counts but never decrement the frequency of any item.
items.scope_note: Contrasts with turnstile updates.

items.name: Linear Bandit
items.definition: An online decision model where reward is a linear function of an unknown parameter and only chosen-action feedback is observed.
items.scope_note: Adversarial versus stochastic rewards and action-set geometry alter regret guarantees.

items.name: Local Edge Differential Privacy
items.definition: A local/distributed privacy notion where an edge's sensitive information is protected through local mechanisms or protocols.
items.scope_note: Different trust and communication assumptions from centralized edge DP.

items.name: LOCAL Model
items.definition: A synchronous distributed graph model with local communication rounds and unbounded messages across each edge per round.
items.scope_note: Usually assumes unique identifiers or a specified symmetry-breaking alternative.

items.name: Mobile Telephone Network Model
items.definition: A peer-to-peer communication abstraction that constrains which pairwise connections devices can form in a communication round.
items.scope_note: Distinct from unrestricted LOCAL and CONGEST message passing models.

items.name: Node Differential Privacy
items.definition: Graph differential privacy where neighboring graphs differ by the presence of a vertex and incident edges.
items.scope_note: Typically a larger perturbation than edge DP; conventions vary.

items.name: Non-Signaling Locality Model
items.definition: A generalized locality model limiting which correlations of local outputs can signal information from distant inputs.
items.scope_note: Formal non-signaling constraints differ from standard message-passing LOCAL.

items.name: Nonclairvoyant Online Model
items.definition: An online information model hiding some job or request characteristics when a decision must be made.
items.scope_note: Specify which parameters are hidden and when feedback arrives.

items.name: Nondeterministic Finite Automaton
items.definition: Finite-state automaton with multiple possible successors for a symbol.
items.scope_note: Equivalent in language recognition power to deterministic finite automata.

items.name: Online Learning
items.definition: An interactive learning model where a learner predicts or chooses actions sequentially while observing feedback and accumulating loss.
items.scope_note: Feedback, adversarial versus stochastic assumptions and comparator class must be stated.

items.name: Optimization Game
items.definition: A cooperative game whose characteristic value for a coalition is given by an underlying optimization problem.
items.scope_note: Different matching, spanning-tree and other optimization games have different payoff allocation conditions.

items.name: PAC Learning
items.definition: A learning model requiring a learner to output a low-error hypothesis with high probability from sufficiently many i.i.d. labeled samples.
items.scope_note: Realizable PAC differs from agnostic PAC learning.

items.name: Persistent Data Structure
items.definition: Data structure retaining access to earlier versions after updates.
items.scope_note: Partial and full persistence permit different operations on past states.

items.name: Point Prediction
items.definition: Advice model supplying one estimated item, location, value or parameter rather than a distribution.
items.scope_note: Prediction distance needs an explicit target and error metric.

items.name: Prediction Portfolio
items.definition: An algorithm receives multiple predictors and can select or combine them during execution.
items.scope_note: Predictor selection and number of predictors affect guarantees.

items.name: Product Distribution
items.definition: A multivariate distribution whose coordinates are mutually independent so its law factors across dimensions.
items.scope_note: Not equivalent to identical coordinate distributions or a known marginal law.

items.name: Prophet Model
items.definition: An online selection model with values drawn from known probability distributions and irrevocable decisions on sequential arrival.
items.scope_note: Independence and arrival order are model assumptions.

items.name: Public-Key Encryption
items.definition: An encryption primitive with a publicly available encryption key and a distinct secret decryption key.
items.scope_note: Security requires formal hardness assumptions and precise adversary models.

items.name: Pushdown Automaton
items.definition: Automaton equipped with an unbounded stack and finite control.
items.scope_note: Nondeterministic PDAs characterize context-free languages; deterministic PDAs are weaker.

items.name: Quantum Circuit Model
items.definition: Quantum model implementing a computation as a sequence of gates on qubits and measurements.
items.scope_note: Gate set, precision, uniformity and measurement conventions matter.

items.name: Quantum Query Model
items.definition: Quantum algorithm model measuring cost in coherent oracle calls.
items.scope_note: Not the same complexity measure as gate count.

items.name: Random Arrival Order
items.definition: An online model receiving an adversarially chosen multiset or collection of inputs in uniformly random order.
items.scope_note: Not independent draws from a distribution; related to but can differ from secretary models.

items.name: Random-Order Model
items.definition: An input model where a fixed collection of requests arrives in a uniformly random permutation.
items.scope_note: Different from independent samples from a distribution.

items.name: Secretary Model
items.definition: An online selection model with adversarial item values arriving in uniformly random order and irrevocable accept/reject decisions.
items.scope_note: The number of selections and objective must be specified.

items.name: Single-Machine Scheduling
items.definition: A scheduling environment where one machine executes jobs subject to stated release, processing and preemption constraints.
items.scope_note: The scheduling environment alone does not determine objective or complexity.

items.name: Stochastic Diffusion Model
items.definition: A random propagation process modeling the spread of a state or infection through a contact network.
items.scope_note: SIR, SIS, independent-cascade and threshold contagion models have different transitions.

items.name: Succinct Data Structure
items.definition: Representation approaching an information-theoretic space bound while supporting efficient operations.
items.scope_note: The combinatorial universe and supported queries must be specified.

items.name: Turing Machine
items.definition: Classical computation model with finite control and a read-write tape.
items.scope_note: Time and space bounds must fix the simulation and input conventions.

items.name: Turnstile Stream
items.definition: A data stream of positive and negative updates to an implicit frequency vector.
items.scope_note: Strict turnstile additionally requires all current frequencies to remain nonnegative.

items.name: Zero-Knowledge Proof
items.definition: A proof system satisfying completeness, soundness and zero-knowledge relative to a chosen model.
items.scope_note: Computational versus statistical zero-knowledge and interaction can differ.

items.name: Makespan Minimization
items.definition: The objective of minimizing the maximum job completion time C_max.
items.scope_note: Completion times depend on the scheduling environment.

items.name: Social Welfare
items.definition: An aggregate objective measuring the value or utility generated by an allocation or joint outcome under a specified welfare aggregation rule.
items.scope_note: Often the sum of agent valuations under quasilinear conventions; distinguish total welfare, Nash welfare and weighted welfare.

items.name: Total Completion Time
items.definition: The objective of minimizing the sum of job completion times over all jobs.
items.scope_note: Weighted completion time is a separate objective.

items.name: Total Cost
items.definition: A social objective aggregating individual or resource costs under a specified model, typically by summing users' experienced costs.
items.scope_note: In routing, standard total latency sums per-path flow times path latency. Maximum individual cost is a different objective.

items.name: Weighted Completion Time
items.definition: The objective of minimizing the sum of w_j C_j over jobs with weights w_j.
items.scope_note: Nonnegative weights and job assumptions matter.

items.name: Art Gallery Problem
items.definition: Place guards within a geometric region so their visibility covers the region using few guards.
items.scope_note: Polygon geometry, allowable guard locations, and approximation criteria matter.

items.name: Automata Emptiness
items.definition: Decide whether a given automaton recognizes any input string.
items.scope_note: Complexity and decidability depend on the automaton model.

items.name: Binary Search
items.definition: Locate a target by adaptive comparisons within a sorted sequence.
items.scope_note: Query model and prediction type determine query complexity.

items.name: Convex Hull
items.definition: Compute the smallest convex set containing a given finite point set, or a representation of its boundary.
items.scope_note: Point dimension and input perturbation model affect sensitivity and complexity.

items.name: Decision Tree Learning
items.definition: Fit an interpretable tree-structured predictor to a labeled dataset while optimizing accuracy or another empirical objective.
items.scope_note: Tree depth, loss, perturbation and training protocol affect stability guarantees.

items.name: Decomposable Submodular Sparsification
items.definition: Approximate a sum of many submodular functions by a weighted sum of relatively few component functions.
items.scope_note: The approximation objective and constraints differ from generic graph sparsification.

items.name: Delaunay Triangulation
items.definition: Construct a triangulation whose simplices satisfy the empty-circumsphere property for a finite point set in general position.
items.scope_note: Degeneracies and ambient dimension require explicit handling.

items.name: Densest Subgraph
items.definition: Choose a nonempty graph vertex subset maximizing a specified density, often induced edges per vertex.
items.scope_note: Graph weights and density normalization matter.

items.name: Distributed Maximal Independent Set
items.definition: Compute an independent set that cannot be enlarged by adding any vertex without violating independence, using local communication.
items.scope_note: Maximal does not mean maximum.

items.name: Distributed Minimum Spanning Tree
items.definition: Find a minimum spanning tree of a connected weighted undirected graph using communication distributed across nodes.
items.scope_note: Round and message complexity depend on communication model, unique weights/IDs and input representation.

items.name: Distributed Vertex Coloring
items.definition: Assign a proper vertex coloring using distributed communication while minimizing rounds and/or colors.
items.scope_note: Round complexity depends on palette and symmetry assumptions.

items.name: Distribution-Free Learning
items.definition: Learn a hypothesis without assuming the unknown data distribution belongs to a specified parametric family.
items.scope_note: Distribution-free sampling still typically assumes i.i.d. examples; agnostic and realizable variants differ.

items.name: Distribution Identity Testing
items.definition: Determine from samples whether an unknown distribution equals a reference or is sufficiently distant.
items.scope_note: Requires a reference representation, support size and distance metric.

items.name: Dynamic Connectivity Query
items.definition: Maintain a graph under edge changes and answer whether vertices are connected.
items.scope_note: Directed and undirected settings differ in complexity.

items.name: Effective Resistance Estimation
items.definition: Estimate the electrical effective resistance between two vertices in a weighted graph.
items.scope_note: Requires conductances and a graph query model; grounded in Laplacian pseudoinverse notions.

items.name: Euclidean k-Clustering
items.definition: Choose k centers in Euclidean space minimizing a specified power of point-to-center distances.
items.scope_note: Includes k-means and k-median-style objectives; metric, dimension and loss exponent matter.

items.name: Fair Division
items.definition: Allocate goods or chores among agents to satisfy a specified fairness criterion.
items.scope_note: Divisibility, sign of valuations and externalities alter feasibility.

items.name: Graph Coloring
items.definition: Assign colors to vertices so adjacent vertices receive different colors, often minimizing the number of colors.
items.scope_note: Number of colors may be part of the input in decision versions.

items.name: Graph Cut
items.definition: Study the edges crossing a vertex partition, with an optimization objective such as minimizing or maximizing crossing weight.
items.scope_note: The cut objective and terminal constraints must be stated.

items.name: Effective Resistance Estimation
items.definition: Approximate the electrical effective resistance between specified nodes in a weighted graph.
items.scope_note: Connectedness, graph weights, precision and local oracle model determine complexity.

items.name: Graph Emulator
items.definition: Construct a sparse graph, not necessarily a subgraph of the input, that approximately preserves pairwise distances.
items.scope_note: Emulators may use new edges/weights; differ from spanners.

items.name: Graph Matching
items.definition: Find a set of graph edges with pairwise disjoint endpoints satisfying a stated optimization or maximality objective.
items.scope_note: Maximum-cardinality matching and inclusion-wise maximal matching are distinct objectives; do not conflate them.

items.name: Graph Property Testing
items.definition: Distinguish a graph having a property from one far from the property using relatively few queries.
items.scope_note: Define graph distance, oracle type, tolerance and error probability.

items.name: Graph Spanner
items.definition: Find or construct a sparse graph substructure that approximately preserves original pairwise distances.
items.scope_note: Specify multiplicative stretch, edge or vertex faults, weights and directedness.

items.name: Heavy Hitters
items.definition: Identify coordinates of a frequency vector with magnitude exceeding a chosen fraction or threshold of total mass.
items.scope_note: L1 and L2 heavy hitters and insertion-only versus turnstile models differ.

items.name: Homomorphism Testing
items.definition: Distinguish structures that avoid a fixed relational homomorphism from structures far from avoiding it by using a limited number of queries.
items.scope_note: The target relational structure and distance/tester access model determine characterization.

items.name: Hopset Optimization
items.definition: Add auxiliary shortcut edges to approximately preserve pairwise distances using few hops while minimizing added edges.
items.scope_note: Stretch, hopbound, directedness and allowed edge weights determine the problem.

items.name: Incremental Knapsack
items.definition: Maintain a feasible high-value knapsack solution as items arrive sequentially.
items.scope_note: Arrival order, feasibility, and the number of solution replacements must be stated.

items.name: Interval Scheduling
items.definition: Select compatible intervals with no temporal overlap to maximize cardinality or total reward.
items.scope_note: Weighted and unweighted variants and tie conventions differ.

items.name: Joint Replenishment with Deadlines
items.definition: Serve requests under deadlines via joint and item-specific replenishment actions with associated costs.
items.scope_note: Clairvoyance of deadlines and ordering constraints are critical.

items.name: Knapsack Problem
items.definition: Given items with values and weights and a capacity budget, select a subset of maximum value whose total weight fits the budget.
items.scope_note: Exact, approximate, online, and bounded-weight variants use different models.

items.name: Language Equivalence
items.definition: Decide whether two formal descriptions recognize the same language.
items.scope_note: Decidable for finite automata; richer grammar models can be undecidable.

items.name: Linearity Testing
items.definition: Test whether an oracle function is linear or far from every linear function.
items.scope_note: Domain, codomain and input distribution are model assumptions.

items.name: Longest Common Subsequence
items.definition: Find a longest sequence occurring as a subsequence of each of two input strings.
items.scope_note: Subsequence is not substring; alphabet and input models can matter.

items.name: Longest Increasing Subsequence
items.definition: Find a longest subsequence of a sequence whose elements are strictly increasing.
items.scope_note: Strict versus non-strict monotonicity and weighted variants need separation.

items.name: Low-Degree Testing
items.definition: Test whether a function is a low-degree polynomial or is far from every such polynomial under a specified distribution.
items.scope_note: Domain, support, degree and oracle access govern query bounds.

items.name: Maximal Matching
items.definition: Find a matching to which no additional edge can be added while preserving vertex-disjointness.
items.scope_note: A maximal matching need not be a maximum-cardinality matching.

items.name: Maximum Clique
items.definition: Find a largest subset of vertices that form a complete graph.
items.scope_note: Do not confuse maximum clique with maximal clique.

items.name: Maximum Coverage
items.definition: Choose at most k sets maximizing the total size or weight of their union.
items.scope_note: Cardinality constraints and coverage objective must be fixed.

items.name: Maximum Cut
items.definition: Partition a graph into two sides to maximize crossing-edge weight.
items.scope_note: Different from the minimum cut objective.

items.name: Maximum Flow
items.definition: Find a feasible source-to-sink flow maximizing total flow value subject to capacity and flow-conservation constraints.
items.scope_note: Standard directed capacitated-network model.

items.name: Maximum Independent Set
items.definition: Find a maximum-cardinality vertex subset containing no adjacent pair.
items.scope_note: The maximum independent set objective should not be confused with maximal independent sets.

items.name: Maximum Matching
items.definition: Find a largest subset of edges sharing no endpoints.
items.scope_note: Maximum cardinality is different from maximality or maximum weight.

items.name: Maximum Weight Chain
items.definition: Find a maximum-weight chain in a partially ordered or transitive directed acyclic graph.
items.scope_note: Graph representation and chain order affect feasible solutions.

items.name: Metric Voting
items.definition: Choose social outcomes using ordinal rankings when true utilities are related to an underlying metric.
items.scope_note: The distortion objective and voter adjacency definitions are essential for privacy analysis.

items.name: Minimum Circuit Size Problem
items.definition: Given the truth table of a Boolean function and size threshold, determine whether the function admits a Boolean circuit below the threshold.
items.scope_note: MCSP is a decision problem central to hardness magnification; circuit basis and encoding matter.

items.name: Minimum Cut
items.definition: Find a cut of minimum total crossing-edge capacity in a specified graph or network.
items.scope_note: Specify undirected/global versus directed s-t version.

items.name: Minimum k-Cut
items.definition: Remove a minimum-weight edge set that leaves at least k connected components.
items.scope_note: Different from multiway cut; fixed and variable k have different regimes.

items.name: Minimum Spanning Forest
items.definition: For each connected component of an undirected weighted graph, compute a minimum-total-weight spanning tree.
items.scope_note: This extends MST to disconnected graphs and is not identical to minimum spanning tree on a disconnected graph.

items.name: Minimum Spanning Tree
items.definition: Find a minimum-weight spanning tree of a connected undirected weighted graph.
items.scope_note: A disconnected graph instead has a spanning forest.

items.name: Minimum Uncut
items.definition: Find a bipartition of graph vertices minimizing the weight of edges whose endpoints lie on the same side.
items.scope_note: Related but not identical to Max-Cut in guarantees under varying normalization.

items.name: Minimum Vertex Cover
items.definition: Given an undirected graph, find a minimum-cardinality vertex set meeting every edge.
items.scope_note: Weighted vertex cover is a separate variant.

items.name: Multiway Cut
items.definition: Find a minimum-weight cut separating a given collection of distinct terminals.
items.scope_note: Terminals and their requirement for separation define the problem.

items.name: Network Capacity
items.definition: Optimize sustained feasible communication throughput under a specified communication and demand model.
items.scope_note: Pairwise, broadcast, all-to-all, reception capacity and wireless interference differ.

items.name: Online Bipartite Matching
items.definition: Match online-arriving vertices to offline vertices without rematching, seeking high matching cardinality or weight.
items.scope_note: Adversarial versus random-order arrivals yield different bounds.

items.name: Online Knapsack
items.definition: Decide whether to accept sequentially arriving weighted/value items under a capacity constraint.
items.scope_note: Profit, arrival process and irrevocability determine online guarantees.

items.name: Online Paging
items.definition: Maintain a bounded cache while handling a sequence of page requests and paying for faults.
items.scope_note: Specified cache capacity and replacement model are essential.

items.name: Online Set Cover
items.definition: Handle elements arriving online by selecting sets irrevocably so that all arrived elements are covered at low cost.
items.scope_note: Clarify fractional vs integral, frequency and recourse model.

items.name: Predecessor Search
items.definition: Find the greatest stored key not exceeding a query key in an ordered universe.
items.scope_note: Universe size, word width and dynamic/static access change bounds.

items.name: Principal Component Analysis
items.definition: Find a low-dimensional subspace capturing maximal sample variance or minimizing squared reconstruction error.
items.scope_note: Centered data, target dimension and online consistency are separate assumptions.

items.name: Private Cut Sparsification
items.definition: Release a sparse approximation to graph cuts while satisfying an explicit graph differential privacy definition.
items.scope_note: Cut approximation may have both multiplicative and additive error; edge privacy model must be fixed.

items.name: Private Minimum Spanning Tree
items.definition: Compute or release an approximate minimum spanning tree under an explicit privacy adjacency and output convention.
items.scope_note: Euclidean data point privacy and general graph edge privacy are different.

items.name: Quantum Search
items.definition: Find a marked item among candidates using a quantum query oracle.
items.scope_note: The search domain, number of solutions and oracle model must be specified.

items.name: Quantum Simulation
items.definition: Approximate quantum-system evolution or observables on a quantum computational device.
items.scope_note: Hamiltonian access, simulation time and error tolerance are essential.

items.name: Shortest Path
items.definition: Find a path with minimum total edge weight between specified vertices.
items.scope_note: Negative weights and cycles change the mathematical guarantees.

items.name: Spectral Clustering
items.definition: Use eigenvectors of a graph Laplacian or similarity matrix to obtain a graph partition or clustering.
items.scope_note: Normalized/unnormalized Laplacian, k and post-processing alter results.

items.name: Spectral Hypergraph Sparsification
items.definition: Construct a sparse weighted hypergraph approximately preserving a chosen hypergraph spectral or energy form.
items.scope_note: Nonlinear hypergraph Laplacians and multiplicative or additive error require explicit definitions.

items.name: Spreading Rule Testing
items.definition: Test whether a dynamic network state evolves according to a specified local propagation rule or is far from it.
items.scope_note: Query access to time states, topology and error/distance model determines bounds.

items.name: Survivable Network Design
items.definition: Find a minimum-cost subgraph meeting prescribed connectivity requirements under failures.
items.scope_note: Terminal pairs, edge/vertex connectivity and relative versus absolute faults vary.

items.name: Tolerant Testing
items.definition: Distinguish inputs close to a property from those significantly farther away.
items.scope_note: Requires two specified distance thresholds.

items.name: Tree Search
items.definition: Find a hidden target vertex in a tree through adaptive queries and path-direction feedback.
items.scope_note: Query feedback and tree structural parameters affect bounds.

items.name: Uniformity Testing
items.definition: Determine from samples whether a discrete distribution is uniform or far from uniform.
items.scope_note: Sample complexity depends on domain size and specified distance.

items.name: Submodular Maximization
items.definition: Maximize a submodular set function under a specified feasibility constraint using value queries or explicit input.
items.scope_note: Monotone, non-monotone, matroid, cardinality and k-submodular variants differ.

items.name: Voronoi Diagram
items.definition: Partition space into regions associated with the nearest input site under a given metric.
items.scope_note: Metric, tie-breaking and dimensionality define the geometry.

items.name: Additive Error
items.definition: An additive deviation between an algorithmic value and a chosen target or optimal benchmark.
items.scope_note: Different from a multiplicative approximation factor and from privacy budget.

items.name: Algorithmic Robustness
items.definition: A formal guarantee that an algorithm maintains bounded performance as an uncertainty or prediction parameter degrades.
items.scope_note: Unlike an informal claim of robustness, must state the exact perturbation family and benchmark.

items.name: Approximate Core
items.definition: A relaxation of the cooperative-game core allowing a controlled multiplicative or additive violation of coalition constraints.
items.scope_note: Characteristic function and exact approximation notion must be specified.

items.name: Approximation Ratio
items.definition: A worst-case guarantee comparing the objective of an algorithmic solution with an optimal solution under a specified minimization or maximization convention.
items.scope_note: Typically rho >= 1 for a minimization approximation; reversed conventions occur.

items.name: Average Algorithmic Sensitivity
items.definition: Average distance between output distributions before and after an elementary input perturbation sampled from a defined distribution.
items.scope_note: Often averaged over deleted graph edges with earth-mover output distance; conventions vary.

items.name: Bipartiteness Ratio
items.definition: A graph conductance-like quantity measuring how close a vertex subset is to supporting a bipartite structure.
items.scope_note: Trevisan-style definitions depend on edge volume and internal/crossing penalties.

items.name: Budget Balance
items.definition: A mechanism property constraining the sum of money collected or transferred across agents.
items.scope_note: Strong and weak budget balance are not the same.

items.name: Centrality Sensitivity
items.definition: Measure how much the numerical centrality score of a vertex or edge changes under graph perturbations.
items.scope_note: It measures centrality-valued changes rather than the Hamming distance of discrete algorithmic solutions.

items.name: Chromatic Number
items.definition: The minimum number of colors in a proper vertex coloring of a graph.
items.scope_note: Integral graph invariant.

items.name: Competitive Ratio
items.definition: A worst-case ratio comparing the cost or reward of an online algorithm to a suitable offline optimum.
items.scope_note: Orientation and any additive constant depend on minimization versus maximization.

items.name: Degree Vector Norm
items.definition: The ℓp norm of a graph's vector of vertex degrees, interpolating between edge-count and maximum-degree objectives.
items.scope_note: p, directionality, graph model and degree normalization must be stated.

items.name: Demographic Parity
items.definition: Require positive prediction rates to be identical across protected groups.
items.scope_note: Does not condition on true outcomes and can conflict with other fairness criteria.

items.name: Differential Privacy
items.definition: A randomized algorithm is differentially private if changing one individual's data changes the probabilities of output events by at most specified multiplicative and possibly additive factors.
items.scope_note: The adjacency relation and privacy parameters epsilon/delta must be specified.

items.name: Distance to Property
items.definition: Minimum normalized modification distance required to satisfy a target property.
items.scope_note: The normalization depends on the model and representation.

items.name: Dynamic Regret
items.definition: Cumulative loss measured against a comparator sequence that may change over time.
items.scope_note: Often depends on a variation/path-length budget.

items.name: EF1
items.definition: For indivisible goods, any envy of another bundle can be eliminated by removing some single item from that other bundle.
items.scope_note: EF1 variants for chores or mixed items need separate definitions.

items.name: EFX
items.definition: For indivisible goods, envy of another bundle disappears after deleting any item in that bundle that the envying agent values positively.
items.scope_note: Distinguish EFX from the stronger EFX0 convention including zero-valued items.

items.name: Envy-Freeness
items.definition: An allocation where every agent values their assigned bundle at least as much as any other agent's bundle.
items.scope_note: Depends on valuation model and whether goods, chores or externalities are present.

items.name: Equality of Opportunity
items.definition: Require equal true-positive rates across protected groups for binary classification.
items.scope_note: One-sided relaxation of equalized odds, not demographic parity.

items.name: Equalized Odds
items.definition: Require identical true-positive and false-positive rates across protected groups in binary classification.
items.scope_note: Conditions on outcome label; differs from demographic parity.

items.name: Fairness Through Awareness
items.definition: Framework enforcing fairness by relating task-specific similarity to output-distribution similarity.
items.scope_note: No unique fairness measure without a defensible similarity metric.

items.name: Fault Budget
items.definition: A bound on the number or nature of edge or vertex failures tolerated while maintaining a required property.
items.scope_note: Fault type, adversarial adaptivity and path/post-fault requirements must be stated.

items.name: Generalization Bound
items.definition: An inequality relating population risk to sample observations with stated probability and hypothesis assumptions.
items.scope_note: Can be uniform, algorithm-dependent or distribution-specific.

items.name: Global Query Sensitivity
items.definition: Largest change in a numeric query over all neighboring pairs of datasets for a selected norm.
items.scope_note: A query-noise calibration parameter, not the algorithmic output-distribution sensitivity.

items.name: Incentive Compatibility
items.definition: A constraint requiring prescribed reporting or strategic behavior to be optimal for agents given the information model.
items.scope_note: DSIC and BIC are different and neither can be assumed from the label alone.

items.name: IND-CPA Security
items.definition: Indistinguishability against chosen-plaintext attacks is a computational confidentiality notion for encryption schemes.
items.scope_note: Chosen-plaintext indistinguishability refers to cryptographic encryption, not differential privacy. Formalize the experiment and adversarial access.

items.name: Individual Fairness
items.definition: Require similar individuals under a task metric to receive similar outcome distributions.
items.scope_note: Choice of task-specific similarity metric is essential.

items.name: Individual Rationality
items.definition: A participation constraint requiring an agent's expected or realized utility to meet their outside-option baseline.
items.scope_note: Specify interim, ex-ante or ex-post participation.

items.name: Influence Maximization
items.definition: An objective measuring total expected spread under a specified stochastic diffusion model and selected initial seeds.
items.scope_note: Diffusion model, seed budget and objective need to be explicit; often formulated as a separate optimization problem.

items.name: Integrality Gap
items.definition: The worst-case ratio between the integral optimum and the relaxation optimum under an explicitly stated objective orientation.
items.scope_note: A property of a particular relaxation and instance family, not an optimization objective.

items.name: Lipschitz Constant
items.definition: Coefficient controlling output change relative to a quantified input change for a chosen algorithm or map.
items.scope_note: Meaningless without specified metrics and perturbation neighborhood.

items.name: Local Query Sensitivity
items.definition: Largest change of a fixed query over datasets adjacent to a specified dataset.
items.scope_note: Dataset-dependent; distinct from global DP sensitivity and randomized algorithmic sensitivity.

items.name: Local Submodularity Ratio
items.definition: Quantify how closely a set function obeys a submodular-type marginal-gain inequality on selected local configurations.
items.scope_note: Not the same as global submodularity or a fixed approximation factor.

items.name: Locality
items.definition: The dependence of a distributed algorithm's decisions on information within some neighborhood radius of each node.
items.scope_note: Radius, model, and whether randomness/identifiers are available must be specified.

items.name: Maximin Share
items.definition: An agent's benchmark obtained by partitioning the items into n bundles and valuing the least desirable bundle under the best possible partition.
items.scope_note: A proportional fairness benchmark, not an assertion that MMS allocations always exist.

items.name: Maximum Degree
items.definition: The greatest number of incident edges at any vertex of a simple graph.
items.scope_note: Degree conventions differ for multigraphs and directed graphs.

items.name: Message Complexity
items.definition: The total number of messages used by a distributed algorithm under its communication model.
items.scope_note: Not determined solely by round complexity.

items.name: Metric Distortion
items.definition: Worst-case ratio comparing social cost of an ordinal voting rule to the optimal alternative given an underlying metric.
items.scope_note: Distortion for randomized rules uses expected cost and its own conventions.

items.name: Nash Social Welfare
items.definition: A welfare objective given by the product of agents' nonnegative utilities, commonly studied for fair allocation.
items.scope_note: Convention for zero utilities and transformations of product versus logarithmic sum must be specified.

items.name: Noise Stability
items.definition: Quantify how strongly a function or model output correlates under specified random perturbations of its inputs.
items.scope_note: Distinct from one-coordinate average sensitivity and algorithmic output stability.

items.name: Online Output Consistency
items.definition: Measure how much a sequence of maintained outputs changes as new input items arrive.
items.scope_note: Requires a distance on outputs and a rule for aggregating changes; not prediction consistency.

items.name: Pareto Optimality
items.definition: No feasible alternative improves one agent without worsening another.
items.scope_note: Efficiency alone does not imply fairness.

items.name: Pointwise Lipschitz Continuity
items.definition: Stable algorithmic behavior quantified by a Lipschitz bound between outputs under changes in input weights or data.
items.scope_note: Requires input and output metrics and coupling conventions.

items.name: Potential Function
items.definition: A real-valued function on system states used to track improvements or quantify progress.

items.name: Prediction Consistency
items.definition: Algorithmic performance guarantee in the case of exact or exceptionally accurate predictions.
items.scope_note: Performance benchmark and additive versus multiplicative convention matter.

items.name: Prediction Error
items.definition: A model-specific distance between the advice and the realized target, instance or distribution.
items.scope_note: Can mean absolute location error, inversions, or Wasserstein distance; must be fixed explicitly.

items.name: Prediction Robustness
items.definition: A performance guarantee that remains bounded under arbitrarily poor predictions.
items.scope_note: Does not imply resistance to arbitrary changes in the computational model.

items.name: Price of Anarchy
items.definition: For a specified class of games, objective, and equilibrium concept, the worst equilibrium-to-optimum ratio in a cost minimization setting, or optimum-to-worst-equilibrium ratio in welfare maximization.
items.scope_note: Requires positive benchmark and precisely defined solution concept; different objective conventions must not be conflated.

items.name: Price of Stability
items.definition: The ratio measuring the efficiency loss of the best equilibrium relative to an optimal feasible outcome in a specified game and objective.
items.scope_note: Best equilibrium need not be unique; existence and objective orientation matter.

items.name: Proportionality
items.definition: Each of n agents receives at least one nth of their value for the complete resource.
items.scope_note: May be infeasible for indivisible goods.

items.name: Query Complexity of Testing
items.definition: Number of oracle queries used by a property tester meeting given completeness and soundness requirements.
items.scope_note: Adaptivity and oracle model must be specified.

items.name: Recourse Bound
items.definition: Bound on the number or cost of modifications to a maintained solution after a data update.
items.scope_note: Not the same as computational update time or differential privacy.

items.name: Regret
items.definition: The cumulative loss of an online learner relative to a chosen benchmark action or policy in hindsight.
items.scope_note: External, swap, dynamic and policy regret are different measures.

items.name: Regret Bound
items.definition: A mathematical guarantee upper-bounding a learner's cumulative regret against a specified comparator class.
items.scope_note: Specify time horizon, learning-rate parameters, adversary assumptions and regret notion.

items.name: Revenue Approximation
items.definition: A guarantee comparing a mechanism's achieved revenue with an optimal reference mechanism or revenue benchmark.
items.scope_note: Depends critically on prior distributions, feasibility constraints, benchmark and incentive constraints.

items.name: Round Complexity
items.definition: The number of synchronous communication rounds required by a distributed algorithm.
items.scope_note: Round count depends on communication model and graph parameters.

items.name: Sample Complexity
items.definition: The minimum number of samples required to meet specified statistical accuracy and confidence requirements.
items.scope_note: Depends on distributional assumptions, learning model and confidence.

items.name: Shannon Entropy
items.definition: Expected information content of a discrete distribution expressed as minus the probability-weighted logarithm.
items.scope_note: Logarithm base affects units; not equivalent to prediction quality.

items.name: Smoothness
items.definition: A deviation inequality with numerical parameters that controls equilibrium inefficiency in a specified class of games.
items.scope_note: A game is smooth only relative to the stated parameters and efficiency objective.

items.name: Solution Stability
items.definition: A requirement that an algorithm output nearby feasible solutions when the input changes slightly.
items.scope_note: Perturbations and output distance require separate definition.

items.name: Spanner Lightness
items.definition: Weight of a distance-preserving spanner relative to an explicitly chosen minimum-weight reference structure.
items.scope_note: For fault-tolerant spanners an MST baseline may be inappropriate; alternative connectivity preservers are used.

items.name: Spanner Stretch
items.definition: Worst-case multiplicative distortion of graph distances when measured in a spanner or emulator.
items.scope_note: Finite distances, failures and weighted/directed conventions matter.

items.name: Spectral Gap
items.definition: An eigenvalue separation associated with a specified graph operator such as its Laplacian or transition matrix.
items.scope_note: Operator, eigenvalue ordering and normalization are essential.

items.name: Stochastic Distance
items.definition: Measure the number or amount of random perturbation required to make a graph likely to satisfy a given property.
items.scope_note: Unlike edit distance, the definition has a probability threshold and a perturbation distribution.

items.name: Tail Risk
items.definition: A probabilistic upper-tail guarantee on an algorithm's realized cost or competitive ratio.
items.scope_note: Fix threshold gamma and maximum allowed violation probability delta.

items.name: Treewidth
items.definition: One less than the maximum bag size in a smallest-width tree decomposition of a graph.
items.scope_note: A structural parameter, not a restriction by itself.

items.name: Truthfulness
items.definition: A reporting incentive property of a mechanism, requiring truthful revelation to optimize utility under a specified notion of incentive compatibility.
items.scope_note: Specify dominant-strategy, ex-post or Bayesian truthfulness; the umbrella term alone is ambiguous.

items.name: VC Dimension
items.definition: The maximum cardinality of a set shattered by a hypothesis class, or infinity if unbounded.
items.scope_note: For binary classification hypotheses.

items.name: Wasserstein Distance
items.definition: An optimal-transport distance between distributions induced by a ground metric.
items.scope_note: Order p and ground metric must be specified; Wasserstein-1 is often called Earth Mover's Distance.

items.name: Welfare Approximation
items.definition: A guarantee comparing a mechanism's produced allocation welfare to a specified optimal welfare benchmark.
items.scope_note: Specify truthfulness, valuation assumptions and approximation orientation.

items.name: Worst-Case Algorithmic Sensitivity
items.definition: The largest output-distribution distance over an allowed family of small input perturbations.
items.scope_note: Yoshida-style output sensitivity is not DP query sensitivity.

items.name: Approximation Algorithm
items.definition: The research task of constructing a polynomial-time algorithm with a stated bounded approximation ratio.
items.scope_note: The guarantee must specify input family and objective.

items.name: Polynomial-Time Algorithm
items.definition: The research task of computing the required result with runtime polynomial in the input encoding length.
items.scope_note: Strong versus weak polynomiality can matter in numerical optimization.

items.name: Tight Lower Bound
items.definition: The research goal of proving a lower bound matching a known upper bound under a precise computational model.
items.scope_note: This is a task label, not a theorem. Complexity assumptions and parameters must be made explicit.

items.name: Amplitude Amplification
items.definition: Increase the success probability of a coherent quantum subroutine through reflections.
items.scope_note: Requires a coherent success predicate and valid inverse circuit.

items.name: Chernoff Bound
items.definition: Exponential tail bounds for sums of independent Bernoulli or related bounded variables.
items.scope_note: Particular versions require independence or other concentration conditions.

items.name: Conditional Value at Risk
items.definition: A downside-risk objective measuring expected loss in a specified worst tail of a probability distribution.
items.scope_note: CVaR is typically an objective or risk measure rather than an algorithm; level alpha must be specified.

items.name: Count-Min Sketch
items.definition: A randomized hash-table sketch used for point-frequency estimates and related streaming queries with additive error guarantees.
items.scope_note: Guarantees depend on frequency norm, nonnegative counts and hash independence.

items.name: Coupling
items.definition: Place multiple random processes in a common probability space for comparison.
items.scope_note: The chosen joint distribution must preserve each process's marginals.

items.name: Cycle Sparsification
items.definition: Reduce graph cycle constraints or represented cycles while maintaining properties needed for approximation and rounding.
items.scope_note: The covering-problem method of Kumabe–Yoshida has scope-specific assumptions.

items.name: Downsampling
items.definition: A sampling-based reduction for testing or learning under high-dimensional product distributions.
items.scope_note: The technique in Harms–Yoshida uses geometric isoperimetry; not arbitrary lossless random subsampling.

items.name: Dynamic Programming
items.definition: Solve overlapping subproblems by storing and combining values or solutions indexed by states.
items.scope_note: State space and transitions determine time and space; not every dynamic program is stable under perturbations.

items.name: Empirical Risk Minimization
items.definition: Choose a hypothesis in a specified class minimizing empirical training loss.
items.scope_note: Generalization needs capacity or stability assumptions.

items.name: Gibbs Sampling
items.definition: Sampling combinatorial solutions with probabilities weighted exponentially by score or energy.
items.scope_note: Temperature, partition function, and sampling runtime must be specified.

items.name: Limited Independence
items.definition: Use k-wise independent random variables instead of fully independent variables.
items.scope_note: Tail bounds depend on independence degree and statistic.

items.name: Linear Programming Relaxation
items.definition: Replace integer or discrete constraints with a linear-programming relaxation to obtain computable bounds or fractional solutions.
items.scope_note: The integrality gap and rounding guarantees depend on the formulation.

items.name: Local Search
items.definition: Iteratively improve a candidate solution using a defined neighborhood until a local optimality criterion holds.
items.scope_note: Approximation guarantees require landscape or exchange properties.

items.name: Locally Testable Code Reduction
items.definition: Use locally testable codes to construct reductions that transfer sensitivity lower bounds to CSP problems.
items.scope_note: Reduction must preserve the perturbation relation and output metric.

items.name: Method of Conditional Expectations
items.definition: Derandomize an expectation argument by fixing choices while maintaining a promising conditional expectation.
items.scope_note: Efficiently computable conditional expectations are usually required.

items.name: Multiplicative Weights Update
items.definition: An online update method that reweights actions exponentially or multiplicatively based on observed losses.
items.scope_note: Regret bounds depend on learning rate and feedback.

items.name: Online Mirror Descent
items.definition: An online optimization update using Bregman divergence to regularize gradient-based steps.
items.scope_note: Performance depends on convexity, geometry and step sizes.

items.name: Phase Estimation
items.definition: Estimate eigenphases of a unitary operator using controlled operations and interference.
items.scope_note: State preparation and precision requirements determine performance.

items.name: Primal-Dual Method
items.definition: Design and analyze algorithms by tracking a primal feasible candidate and a related dual certificate.
items.scope_note: The concrete dual and complementary-slackness reasoning vary by problem.

items.name: Privacy Amplification by Subsampling
items.definition: A privacy technique using random subsampling to reduce the effective information exposure of an analysis.
items.scope_note: Amplification bounds depend on sampling scheme, adjacency and base mechanism.

items.name: Private Expander Decomposition
items.definition: A graph decomposition technique implemented under differential privacy to support accurate cut sparsification.
items.scope_note: Decomposition guarantees, privacy model and sparsification error are paper-specific.

items.name: Probabilistic Method
items.definition: Use positive probability of a desirable random outcome to prove an object exists.
items.scope_note: Existence alone is not an efficient algorithm.

items.name: Quantum Error Correction
items.definition: Encode quantum information redundantly so specified errors can be detected or corrected.
items.scope_note: Specify code, noise model and fault-tolerance assumptions.

items.name: Quantum Fourier Transform
items.definition: Perform the discrete Fourier transform unitarily on quantum computational-basis amplitudes.
items.scope_note: Complexity depends on register size and approximation precision.

items.name: Randomized Rounding
items.definition: Randomly transform a fractional solution into a discrete solution while controlling feasibility and expected objective.
items.scope_note: Only applicable after specifying a relaxation and dependent or independent rounding scheme.

items.name: Regularized Linear Programming
items.definition: Solve an optimization relaxation with an additional regularizer that encourages stable outputs.
items.scope_note: Strong convexity, norm, and rounding determine the Lipschitz guarantee.

items.name: Semidefinite Programming Relaxation
items.definition: Relax a discrete optimization problem to a semidefinite program involving positive-semidefinite matrix variables.
items.scope_note: Guarantees depend on the particular SDP and rounding procedure.
